# statuspage_page (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
# Pages cannot be created or deleted through the Statuspage API — only read
# and updated. This resource can only attach to a page that already exists;
# see import.sh in this directory. `terraform destroy` (or removing the
# block) only forgets the page in Terraform state; the page itself is left
# untouched.
resource "statuspage_page" "my_page" {
  page_id = "my_page_id"

  name      = "My Status Page"
  time_zone = "Berlin" # Rails ActiveSupport name, not IANA (not "Europe/Berlin")

  # Changing domain makes Statuspage start certificate provisioning for the
  # new host, which this API cannot observe — the CNAME must already point
  # at Statuspage's edge before this is set.
  domain = "status.example.com"

  hidden_from_search        = false
  allow_email_subscribers   = true
  allow_sms_subscribers     = false
  allow_webhook_subscribers = false

  css_link_color = "3498DB"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `page_id` (String) The Statuspage page code (e.g. `abc123def456`, from the manage.statuspage.io URL). Pages cannot be created or deleted through the API, so this must name an existing page; bring it under management with `terraform import` or an `import {}` block.

### Optional

- `allow_email_subscribers` (Boolean) Allow visitors to receive notifications via email.
- `allow_incident_subscribers` (Boolean) Allow visitors to subscribe to notifications for a single incident.
- `allow_page_subscribers` (Boolean) Allow visitors to subscribe to all notifications on the page.
- `allow_rss_atom_feeds` (Boolean) Allow visitors to access incident feeds via RSS/Atom (not functional on audience-specific pages).
- `allow_sms_subscribers` (Boolean) Allow visitors to receive notifications via SMS.
- `allow_webhook_subscribers` (Boolean) Allow visitors to receive notifications via webhooks.
- `branding` (String) Page template: `basic` or `premium`. The API rejects `premium` on plans that don't offer it.
- `css_blues` (String) CSS color: maintenance status indicator.
- `css_body_background_color` (String) CSS color: page body background.
- `css_border_color` (String) CSS color: borders.
- `css_font_color` (String) CSS color: main font.
- `css_graph_color` (String) CSS color: uptime/metrics graphs.
- `css_greens` (String) CSS color: operational status indicator.
- `css_light_font_color` (String) CSS color: secondary/light font.
- `css_link_color` (String) CSS color: links.
- `css_no_data` (String) CSS color: graph areas with no data.
- `css_oranges` (String) CSS color: partial-outage status indicator.
- `css_reds` (String) CSS color: major-outage status indicator.
- `css_yellows` (String) CSS color: degraded-performance status indicator.
- `domain` (String) Custom domain (CNAME host) serving the page, e.g. `status.example.com`. Changing this makes Statuspage start certificate provisioning and domain validation for the new host — a flow the API does not expose, so it is invisible to Terraform: `apply` can report success while issuance still fails server-side. The CNAME must already point at the Statuspage edge before this is set.
- `hidden_from_search` (Boolean) Whether the page hides itself from search engines.
- `name` (String) Name of the page as displayed to visitors.
- `notifications_email_footer` (String) Footer appended to notification emails. Accepts Markdown.
- `notifications_from_email` (String) From-address for page notification emails.
- `subdomain` (String) The `*.statuspage.io` subdomain. Changing it changes the page's canonical URL — treat as risky.
- `time_zone` (String) Timezone for the page, in Rails ActiveSupport form (e.g. `Berlin`, `UTC`) — not IANA (`Europe/Berlin`, `Etc/UTC`).
- `url` (String) The website linked from the page's logo/image — not the status page's own public address (the API has no field for that). It may coincidentally equal the public URL without being derived from it.
- `viewers_must_be_team_members` (Boolean) Restrict page visibility to team members only.

### Read-Only

- `activity_score` (Number) Statuspage's internal activity score for the page. Read-only.
- `city` (String) City shown on the page. Read-only through this API.
- `country` (String) Country shown on the page. Read-only through this API.
- `created_at` (String) Timestamp the page was created (RFC3339).
- `headline` (String) Page headline. Read-only through this API.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ip_restrictions` (String) IP restriction list. Read-only through this API.
- `page_description` (String) Page description. Read-only through this API.
- `state` (String) State/region shown on the page. Read-only through this API.
- `support_url` (String) Support URL shown on the page. Read-only through this API — changed in the UI, it moves in state with no way to drive it from config.
- `twitter_username` (String) Twitter/X username shown on the page. Read-only through this API.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp the page was last updated (RFC3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Pages cannot be created via the API, so this is the only way to bring one
# under management — the import ID is just the page code, not a composite
# "page_id/id" like statuspage_component and friends use.
terraform import statuspage_page.my_page my_page_id
```
